title: Crohn's, ulcerative colitis, IBS and pancreatitis
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's digestive condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for management of chronic pancreatitis.

HPI
The patient is a 50-year-old male presenting for a routine follow-up regarding his chronic pancreatitis. He reports that his symptoms have been well-controlled since his last visit. He continues to experience occasional abdominal discomfort but notes that his appetite remains stable. He reports that he is adherent to his current regimen of pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy and has not experienced any significant weight loss or severe flares of pain. He denies any new symptoms or concerns at this time.

Medication List
- Pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy (PERT)
- Omeprazole 20mg daily

Exam
The patient appears well-nourished and in no acute distress. Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. Bowel sounds are present in all quadrants. Vital signs are stable and within normal limits.

Assessment
1. Chronic pancreatitis: Stable and well-managed with current enzyme replacement therapy.

Plan
1. Continue current dose of pancreatic enzyme replacement therapy with meals and snacks.
2. Follow up in six months for a routine evaluation of his chronic pancreatitis.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, PA-C, 05/12/2026

distractors.why: The pancreatitis is chronic and current.
Chronic pancreatitis is K86.1, not acute pancreatitis.
